name: Emma Fourreau - Projet de décision du Conseil
title: RECOMMENDATION on the proposal for a Council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the European Union, of the Implementing Protocol (2025-2030) to the Sustainable Fisheries Partnership Agreement between the European Union and the Government of Greenland and the Government of Denmark
part_text:
The European Parliament agrees to a new six-year deal letting around ten European Union fishing boats catch cod, Greenland halibut, redfish and Northern prawn in Greenland's waters. In return, the European Union pays about 17.3 million euros a year: 14.1 million for fishing access and 3.2 million to support Greenland's fisheries policy, plus fees from boat owners. The deal runs from 2025 to 2030. Parliament also asks for better data, respect for scientific advice, and protection of the Arctic marine environment.

- What changes: European Union boats keep fishing rights in Greenland's waters until 2030, with more money for Greenland.
- Who it affects: Greenland's coastal and Inuit communities, European fishing crews, and Arctic sea life.
- What happens next: the deal applies provisionally; Parliament's consent lets it be formally concluded.
